functions.name: C
functions.summary: Computes the normalized Fresnel cosine integral.
description: C(x) represents integral(cos(pi*t^2/2), t, 0, x). Numeric real arguments are evaluated numerically; symbolic arguments remain as C(x).

examples.description: Evaluate the normalized Fresnel cosine integral at zero.
Keep a symbolic argument symbolic.

functions.name: S
functions.summary: Computes the normalized Fresnel sine integral.
description: S(x) represents integral(sin(pi*t^2/2), t, 0, x). Numeric real arguments are evaluated numerically; symbolic arguments remain as S(x).

examples.description: Evaluate the normalized Fresnel sine integral at zero.
Keep a symbolic argument symbolic.

functions.name: realpart
functions.summary: Returns the real component of a complex expression.
description: Nerdamer expands supported algebraic structure and separates known real and complex factors. Expressions whose complex component cannot yet be resolved can remain under realpart(...).

examples.description: Extract the real component of a numeric complex value.
Expand a symbolic complex product and collect its real component.

functions.name: imagpart
functions.summary: Returns the imaginary component of a complex expression.
description: Nerdamer expands supported algebraic structure and separates known real and complex factors. Purely real expressions return zero; unresolved complex functions can remain under imagpart(...).

examples.description: Extract the imaginary coefficient.
Expand a symbolic complex product and collect its imaginary component.

functions.name: arg
functions.summary: Returns the principal argument of a complex expression.
description: The argument is computed from the real and imaginary components using quadrant-aware atan2 behavior. Pure imaginary axis cases are handled explicitly.

examples.description: Return the principal angle of 1+i.
Keep the quadrant of a symbolic imaginary coefficient explicit.

functions.name: conjugate
functions.summary: Returns the complex conjugate of an expression.
description: Conjugation changes i to -i and distributes through supported sums, products, and powers when the transformation is valid for the represented branch.
The same operation is available directly as nerdamer.conjugate(...).

examples.description: Conjugate a symbolic rectangular complex expression.
Conjugate the imaginary unit.

functions.name: csgn
functions.summary: Returns the complex sign used by Nerdamer's branch-sensitive simplification rules.
description: csgn returns 1 when the real part is positive and -1 when the real part is negative. If the real part is zero, it uses the sign of the imaginary part. Zero returns 0.
When the sign cannot be determined symbolically, Nerdamer keeps csgn(...) unevaluated. The same operation is available directly as nerdamer.csgn(...).

examples.description: Use the sign of a positive real part.
Use the sign of a negative real part.
Keep an unresolved symbolic complex sign.

functions.name: polarform
functions.summary: Converts a complex expression toward polar exponential form.
description: Nerdamer derives a magnitude and principal argument, then represents the result using r*e^(i*theta) when conversion is meaningful. Already simple real or purely imaginary linear values may remain compact.

examples.description: Derive an exact magnitude and symbolic principal argument.

functions.name: rectform
functions.summary: Converts supported polar complex forms toward rectangular form.
description: Nerdamer recognizes exponential polar forms and rewrites them with cosine and sine components. If no exact identity is available, an evaluable complex expression can be returned in rectangular form.

examples.description: Convert an exact polar exponential back to rectangular form.

functions.name: abs
functions.summary: Computes the absolute value of an expression.
description: Nerdamer simplifies absolute values when sign information is available from numbers, algebraic structure, or assumptions. Even powers are recognized as non-negative, while genuinely sign-unknown expressions remain wrapped in abs.
For complex inputs, absolute value is the complex modulus.

examples.description: Take the absolute value of a negative number.
Recognize an even power as non-negative.
Use an assumption to determine the sign of an affine expression.

functions.name: cbrt
functions.summary: Computes the cube root of an expression.
description: Ordinary parsing preserves cbrt as a function node instead of forcing numerical evaluation, which avoids changing branch behavior or introducing unnecessary approximation.
Call evaluate() when a numeric value is required. Real numeric arguments then use the real cube root, so negative reals remain real; complex arguments use the principal cube root.

examples.description: Keep the cube root symbolic until evaluation is requested.
Preserve the real negative cube-root expression during ordinary parsing.
Keep a symbolic cube root.

functions.name: ceil
functions.summary: Rounds a numeric expression up to the nearest integer.
description: Numeric inputs return the least integer greater than or equal to the value. Symbolic inputs remain as ceil(x).
The compatibility spelling ceiling is an alias of ceil.

examples.description: Round a positive decimal upward.
Round a negative decimal toward positive infinity.

functions.name: contains
functions.summary: Tests membership in a supported finite container.
description: Vector membership compares elements, finite sets and solution sets use set membership, and Dictionary membership checks keys. The result is 1 when present and 0 when absent.
Unsupported container types remain as a symbolic contains(container,value) call.

examples.description: Find a value in a vector.
Return zero when the value is absent.

functions.name: numeric
functions.summary: Evaluates a numeric value to a finite number of significant decimal digits.
description: numeric(value[,precision]) is the explicit finite-precision evaluation boundary. It evaluates fully numeric input and returns decimal-origin values at the requested significant-digit precision.
Symbolic results remain symbolic rather than having individual symbolic coefficients approximated. The full JavaScript / TypeScript package also exposes nerdamer.numeric(...).

examples.description: Evaluate a rational value to five significant digits.
Apply finite-precision evaluation to a structured value.

functions.name: size
functions.summary: Returns the dimensions of a structured parser value.
description: size(...) reports the public dimensions of vectors, matrices, sets, collections, and dictionaries.
The result is returned as a Vector of dimension sizes.

examples.description: Return the length of a Vector.
Return matrix row and column counts.

functions.name: count
functions.summary: Returns the number of entries in a supported container.
description: count evaluates Vectors, finite value sets, solution sets, and Dictionaries. Other inputs remain as a symbolic count(...) call.

examples.description: Count vector elements.

functions.name: exp
functions.summary: Computes the exponential function e raised to an expression.
description: exp(x) is represented using Nerdamer's symbolic exponential form. Exact simplifications are applied where available, and numeric inputs can be evaluated.

examples.description: Evaluate e^0.
Keep a symbolic exponential.

functions.name: expand
functions.summary: Expands an expression algebraically.
description: expand distributes products over sums, expands supported integer powers, and recursively expands algebraic structure. It is useful when a multiplied or powered form needs to be rewritten as an explicit sum of terms.
Expansion does not mean numerical evaluation; symbols and supported functions remain symbolic.

examples.description: Expand a binomial power exactly.
Distribute a symbolic product and collect the result.

functions.name: floor
functions.summary: Rounds a numeric expression down to the nearest integer.
description: Numeric inputs return the greatest integer less than or equal to the value. Symbolic inputs remain as floor(x).

examples.description: Round a positive decimal downward.
Round a negative decimal toward negative infinity.

functions.name: log
functions.summary: Computes the natural logarithm or a logarithm with an explicit base.
description: With one argument, log uses base e. An optional second argument selects a base. Exact integer-base powers and common symbolic forms are simplified when safe.
Complex inputs use the principal logarithm, and real-domain logarithm rewrites are only applied when their sign requirements are established.

examples.description: Evaluate the natural logarithm of e.
Evaluate an exact logarithm with base 2.
Keep a symbolic logarithm.

functions.name: matrix
functions.summary: Constructs a matrix from row vectors.
description: Each argument supplies one row. Rows must have matching lengths, and their elements are converted to Nerdamer expressions.
The result is a Matrix entity that can be used by determinant, matrix methods, and other linear-algebra operations.

examples.description: Construct a 2 by 2 matrix.

functions.name: max
functions.summary: Returns the greatest value when the arguments can be ordered.
description: Numeric and otherwise comparable arguments are reduced to the maximum. If Nerdamer cannot establish an ordering between symbolic arguments, the unresolved part remains symbolic.
Available assumptions can help determine ordering for symbolic values.

examples.description: Select the largest numeric argument.
Use assumptions to order symbolic arguments.

functions.name: min
functions.summary: Returns the smallest value when the arguments can be ordered.
description: Numeric and otherwise comparable arguments are reduced to the minimum. If Nerdamer cannot establish an ordering between symbolic arguments, the unresolved part remains symbolic.
Available assumptions can help determine ordering for symbolic values.

examples.description: Select the smallest numeric argument.
Use assumptions to order symbolic arguments.

functions.name: nthroot
functions.summary: Computes the nth root as a principal fractional power.
description: nthroot(x,n) is represented as x^(1/n), so branch behavior follows Nerdamer's power rules. Use cbrt when the real cube root of a negative real is specifically required.

examples.description: Take a fourth root using the principal power.
Keep a symbolic root degree.

functions.name: parens
functions.summary: Wraps an expression in explicit parentheses for output.
description: parens creates a grouping node whose main purpose is preserving visible parentheses in formatted output. It does not change the mathematical value of the wrapped expression.

examples.description: Preserve explicit grouping around a sum.

functions.name: round
functions.summary: Rounds a number to a requested number of decimal places.
description: With no second argument, round uses integer precision. An optional integer precision selects decimal places. Symbolic values or unsupported precisions remain symbolic.

examples.description: Round to the nearest integer.
Round to two decimal places.

functions.name: sign
functions.summary: Returns the sign of a real expression when it can be determined.
description: The result is 1, -1, or 0 for known positive, negative, or zero values. Assumptions can resolve symbolic signs; otherwise sign(x) remains symbolic.
Complex inputs are delegated to the complex sign function.

examples.description: Identify a positive number.
Identify a negative number.
Infer the sign of a symbolic affine expression from an assumption.

functions.name: sqrt
functions.summary: Computes the principal square root of an expression.
description: Square roots are represented through a one-half power and simplified with Nerdamer's radical rules. Perfect squares and compatible radical products are reduced exactly.
For symbolic squares, sign information matters: without a sign assumption sqrt(x^2) simplifies to abs(x).

examples.description: Reduce a perfect square exactly.
Return the exact principal complex square root.
Preserve the sign ambiguity of a symbolic square.
Use a known lower bound to resolve the sign of a shifted square.

functions.name: subst
functions.summary: Substitutes one expression for another inside an expression tree.
description: subst(expression,value,replacement) replaces matching variables or supported compound subexpressions while preserving the surrounding symbolic structure. The substitution recurses into sums, products, functions, and powers.
It can replace more than a single symbol when the requested subexpression can be matched structurally.

examples.description: Replace a variable throughout nested structure.
Replace a complete subexpression.

functions.name: trunc
functions.summary: Truncates a numeric expression toward zero.
description: Numeric inputs discard the fractional part without changing the sign of the integer portion. Symbolic inputs remain as trunc(x).

examples.description: Discard a positive fractional part.
Truncate a negative number toward zero.

functions.name: div
functions.summary: Performs polynomial division and returns quotient and remainder.
description: When both arguments are polynomial-like, div returns a two-element Vector containing the quotient and remainder. Inputs outside the polynomial domain use the compatibility fallback [0, dividend].
Multivariable input is handled as a multivariable polynomial rather than by silently choosing one main variable.

examples.description: Return the exact polynomial quotient together with a zero remainder.

functions.name: divide
functions.summary: Divides expressions using polynomial quotient/remainder reconstruction when possible.
description: For polynomial inputs, divide reconstructs quotient+remainder/divisor as a reusable Expression. Inputs outside the polynomial domain fall back to ordinary symbolic division.
Unlike div, the result is a single expression rather than a quotient/remainder Vector.

examples.description: Reconstruct an exact polynomial quotient.

functions.name: polyFactors
functions.summary: Returns polynomial factors as a Vector of separate factor expressions.
description: In Nerdamer Notation, use polyfactors(...). In JavaScript or TypeScript, use polyFactors(...) from the root API or nerdamer/algebra.
The result is a Vector containing the factor expressions rather than a single product.

examples.description: Return the factors of a difference of squares as separate Vector entries.

functions.name: forget
functions.summary: Removes stored assumptions for a symbol or clears all assumptions.
description: forget(x) removes the current assumption for x. The special form forget(all) clears the complete assumption store.

examples.description: Remove the stored assumption for x.
Clear all stored assumptions.

functions.name: unassign
functions.summary: Removes a parser-known value assigned to a variable.
description: unassign restores a known parser variable to its unassigned symbolic form. It affects assigned values, not the separate assumption store.

examples.description: Remove a parser assignment and recover the symbol.

functions.name: factor
functions.summary: Factors an expression into a product of simpler factors.
description: Use factor to expose multiplicative structure in polynomial-like expressions. It can factor univariate and multivariate polynomials, extract common factors, recognize repeated factors, and prime-factor exact integers.
If Nerdamer cannot factor an input using its supported symbolic methods, the expression may remain unchanged or as an unevaluated factor call.

examples.description: Factor a quadratic over the integers.
Recognize a multivariable perfect square.
Prime-factor an exact integer.

functions.name: simplify
functions.summary: Rewrites an expression into a simpler equivalent form using Nerdamer's symbolic simplification rules.
description: Simplification includes algebraic cancellation, polynomial and rational reduction, selected identities, factorial cancellation, radical simplification, and simplification inside function arguments.
The result remains symbolic. Nerdamer only applies transformations it can justify from the expression and any available assumptions.

examples.description: Cancel a common polynomial factor.
Apply a trigonometric identity.
Cancel adjacent factorials symbolically.

functions.name: gcd
functions.summary: Returns the greatest common divisor of two symbolic expressions when their polynomial structure can be resolved.
description: Nerdamer preserves common numeric, monomial, univariate, and multivariable polynomial factors. Rational polynomial structure is normalized before the common divisor is computed.
If the supported polynomial methods cannot resolve the inputs, the operation can remain symbolic as gcd(a,b).

examples.description: Keep the common numeric and polynomial factor.
Extract a common multivariable monomial.
Preserve a common factor containing symbolic parameters.

functions.name: lcm
functions.summary: Returns the least common multiple of two expressions.
description: Numeric inputs use exact rational arithmetic. For symbolic polynomial expressions, Nerdamer computes the product divided by the symbolic greatest common divisor so shared factors are retained.
If either operand is zero, the result is zero.

examples.description: Compute an exact integer least common multiple.
Retain the shared polynomial factor once while combining the distinct factors.
Apply the zero case.

functions.name: groebner
functions.summary: Computes a Gröbner basis for a polynomial system.
description: The public function accepts a collection of polynomial expressions and returns the resulting basis as a Vector. The default public basis uses lexicographic ordering, and the JavaScript / TypeScript API can also receive an explicit variable order.
A Gröbner basis can expose elimination structure or rewrite a polynomial system into an equivalent form that is easier to analyze.

examples.description: Rewrite a circle-line system into a triangular form.
Compute the Cyclic-3 basis.

functions.name: partfrac
functions.summary: Decomposes a rational expression into partial fractions with respect to a variable.
description: Nerdamer handles rational expressions with distinct or repeated linear factors, supported irreducible quadratic factors, and improper fractions that first require polynomial division.
When no useful decomposition is available, the original expression is returned unchanged.

examples.description: Decompose a rational function with two distinct linear factors.
Reduce an improper rational expression when the remainder is zero.
Decompose a denominator containing a repeated linear factor.

functions.name: completeSquare
functions.summary: Rewrites a quadratic in completed-square form.
description: Use sqcomp(...) in Nerdamer Notation. In JavaScript or TypeScript, completeSquare(...) returns the completed-square expression together with the quadratic coefficient, shift, remainder, and selected variable.
The direct API is available from the root nerdamer export and from nerdamer/algebra.

examples.description: Rewrite a quadratic as a shifted square plus a constant.

notes: The parser form returns the completed-square expression. The JavaScript / TypeScript completeSquare(...) helper returns a CompleteSquareResult object whose expression field contains that expression.

functions.name: content
functions.summary: Returns the exact numeric content of a polynomial.
description: The content is the greatest common divisor of the polynomial's numeric coefficients. It is a numeric coefficient measure, not a polynomial-valued greatest common divisor of symbolic coefficient expressions.
If the input cannot be converted to a polynomial, the operation remains symbolic.

examples.description: Extract the greatest common divisor of the coefficients.
Return 1 when the coefficients are primitive.

functions.name: deg
functions.summary: Returns the degree of a polynomial expression.
description: With no variable argument, deg returns the total degree: the largest sum of powers in any term. With a variable, it returns the largest power of that variable while treating other variables as coefficients.
If the input cannot be converted to a polynomial, the operation remains symbolic.

examples.description: Return the total degree of a multivariable polynomial.
Return the degree with respect to x.
Return the degree with respect to y.

functions.name: solve
functions.summary: Solves an expression or equation for a variable and returns the solutions as a SolutionSet.
description: Nerdamer's solver is not limited to polynomial roots. It combines exact symbolic isolation, polynomial solving, supported radical and rational transformations, complex arithmetic, periodic families, and numerical root finding for equations that do not reduce to a closed symbolic form.

Expressions are treated as equations equal to zero; explicit equations can be supplied directly. Candidate roots are checked against the source equation in supported transformations so denominator singularities and extraneous roots introduced while isolating radicals or logarithms can be rejected.
The solver returns distinct solutions in a SolutionSet rather than a plain JavaScript array.

examples.description: Derive the quadratic formula while preserving symbolic parameters.
Return the complete periodic family. _n is Nerdamer's reserved integer index, so this represents x=n*pi for every integer n.
Store the periodic SolutionSet, then evaluate the family at n=0 with a substitution local to evaluate. Use : to assign sol; = constructs an equation.
Invert an exponential with a symbolic compound base; the result is equivalent to log(y)/log(a+b).
Solve a rational-transcendental equation while excluding x=0, where the original denominator vanishes.
Isolate a radical and verify the surviving branch against the original equation.
Solve a logarithmic equation and reject roots that violate the original logarithm domains.
Solve directly over complex values.
Find both real roots when the unknown also appears in an exponent, including the nontrivial numerical root near 0.309906932380691 and the exact root 4.
Isolate velocity in the relativistic kinetic-energy equation and return the two symbolic velocity branches.

notes: _n is Nerdamer's reserved integer family parameter. In {_n*pi}, substituting _n=-2,-1,0,1,2,... gives ..., -2*pi, -pi, 0, pi, 2*pi, ... and therefore all roots of sin(x)=0.

In Nerdamer Scripting, a periodic SolutionSet can be stored and evaluated with sol: solve(sin(x),x); evaluate(sol,{_n=>0}), which returns {0}. The : operator stores sol; = denotes an equation and is not assignment syntax.
The {_n=>0} Dictionary entry is local to evaluate. It does not assign the reserved _n name globally, so _n:0 remains invalid.

To select a member of a periodic family in JavaScript / TypeScript, take the returned family expression and substitute an integer for _n: const solutions = nerdamer.solve('sin(x)', 'x'); const family = solutions.elements[0]; family.subst('_n', 2).text() returns 2*pi.
Some non-polynomial equations require numerical root finding; those solutions can therefore be approximate rather than exact symbolic expressions.

functions.name: solveSystem
functions.summary: Solves linear, nonlinear, symbolic, and supported non-polynomial systems and returns solution assignments.
description: System solving goes well beyond square linear systems. Nerdamer can preserve free variables in underdetermined linear systems, accept consistent overdetermined systems, solve supported nonlinear polynomial systems exactly, retain irrational and complex solutions, and fall back to numerical multivariate solving for supported systems containing functions such as trigonometric expressions.

Nerdamer Notation uses solveeqs(...). The JavaScript / TypeScript API uses solveSystem(...) and can additionally receive an explicit variable order, which is useful when other symbols should be treated as parameters rather than unknowns.

Solutions are returned as dictionaries inside a Vector. Nonlinear solving can return several isolated assignments, while underdetermined linear systems express pivot variables in terms of the remaining free variables.

examples.description: Solve an underdetermined linear system and retain z as a free variable.
Find both exact intersections of a parabola and a line: (-1,1) and (2,4).
Solve a nonlinear geometric system exactly, preserving the two irrational circle-line intersections.
Solve a nonlinear three-variable system with six isolated solutions.
Use numerical multivariate solving for a mixed trigonometric-polynomial system; the real solutions are approximately x=±2.68259128682539 and y=-0.196296012151496.
Solve a linear system whose coefficients and solutions are complex.
Accept a consistent overdetermined system instead of requiring exactly one equation per unknown.
Clear a rational denominator while preserving the valid exact system solution.
Solve a system containing a transcendental function numerically rather than rejecting it as non-polynomial.

notes: Underdetermined linear systems are parameterized using their free variables. Nonlinear systems with a non-isolated infinite solution set are not currently represented this way and can throw an UnsupportedOperationError.

Numerical multivariate solving returns roots found within the solver's search strategy; it does not turn a periodic function such as sin(x)=0 into an infinite symbolic family. Use solve(...) for symbolic periodic families when solving a single equation.
Use solveSystem(equations, variables) in JavaScript / TypeScript when the unknown-variable list must be supplied explicitly.

functions.name: diff
functions.summary: Differentiates an expression symbolically with respect to a variable.
description: Nerdamer applies the standard differentiation rules to algebraic expressions and supported functions, including product, quotient, power, and chain rules. Higher-order derivatives can be requested with the optional order argument.

examples.description: Differentiate a polynomial.
Apply the chain rule through a trigonometric power.
Differentiate a variable raised to a variable-dependent power.

functions.name: integrate
functions.summary: Computes a symbolic antiderivative with respect to a variable when Nerdamer has a supported integration path.
description: Integration handles linear combinations, constant factors, common elementary functions, scaled arguments, and a broader set of algebraic and trigonometric forms through Nerdamer's integration routines.
When an antiderivative is not available, Nerdamer can leave the integral unevaluated instead of inventing a result.

examples.description: Integrate a polynomial term by term.
Use linearity across elementary functions.
Account for a scaled inner argument.

functions.name: limit
functions.summary: Computes a symbolic limit of an expression as a variable approaches a value.
description: Nerdamer first uses direct evaluation where possible, then applies symbolic strategies for supported indeterminate forms and common rational, logarithmic, and exponential growth patterns. One-sided limits are available through the optional direction argument.
When the limit cannot be resolved by the supported methods, the operation remains symbolic.

examples.description: Resolve the standard removable singularity at zero.
Compare leading polynomial terms at infinity.
Recognize that linear growth dominates logarithmic growth.

functions.name: laplace
functions.summary: Computes the symbolic Laplace transform of an expression.
description: The transform maps an expression from a source variable to a transform variable. Supported forms include powers, exponentials, trigonometric and hyperbolic functions, linear combinations, and common shift and scaling patterns.
If no supported transform rule applies, Nerdamer leaves the Laplace transform unevaluated.

examples.description: Transform a polynomial power.
Apply the exponential shift rule exactly.
Transform a trigonometric function symbolically.

functions.name: ilaplace
functions.summary: Computes a symbolic inverse Laplace transform of an expression.
description: The inverse transform handles common rational forms, repeated poles, shifted linear and quadratic factors, and supported trigonometric and hyperbolic transform pairs.
If Nerdamer cannot resolve the inverse transform, it leaves the ilaplace call unevaluated.

examples.description: Invert a repeated shifted pole.
Invert a repeated pole at -1.
Recover a damped sinusoid from an irreducible quadratic.

functions.name: sum
functions.summary: Evaluates a finite symbolic sum over an integer index.
description: With concrete integer bounds, Nerdamer substitutes the index through the inclusive range and adds the resulting symbolic terms. If a bound is still symbolic, the sum remains unevaluated.

examples.description: Sum a simple finite integer range.
Combine symbolic indexing, a Vector, size(...), and a finite sum.
Substitute a finite integer range through an expression with symbolic parameters.

functions.name: product
functions.summary: Evaluates a finite symbolic product over an integer index.
description: With concrete integer bounds, Nerdamer substitutes the index through the inclusive range and multiplies the resulting symbolic terms. If a bound is still symbolic, the product remains unevaluated.

examples.description: Multiply a simple finite integer range.
Build an exact symbolic product of shifted factors.
Multiply indexed symbolic Vector entries over their full range.

functions.name: defint
functions.summary: Evaluates a definite integral over an interval.
description: Nerdamer uses symbolic integration when available and can use numerical evaluation for supported numeric bounds. Symbols that are independent of the integration variable are treated as constants.
Supplying the integration variable explicitly avoids ambiguity in expressions containing more than one symbol.

examples.description: Evaluate a simple polynomial definite integral with numeric bounds.
Evaluate the singular-endpoint integral numerically; the result is approximately -1.
Keep parameters that are independent of the integration variable.

functions.name: assume
functions.summary: Adds a real numeric interval assumption for a symbol so assumption-aware operations can use the known range.
description: Assumptions narrow a plain variable to a non-empty interval of real numeric values. Repeated constraints for the same variable are intersected, and contradictory constraints are rejected without replacing the previous assumption.
Assumptions are used conservatively. They can influence comparisons and transformations that depend on sign or ordering, but they are not a general logical theorem system.

examples.description: Use disjoint symbolic ranges to prove which variable is larger.
Use a lower bound to remove an otherwise necessary absolute value.
Use positivity information in a sign-sensitive logarithm simplification.

notes: The direct string API accepts a variable, a comparison operator, and a numeric bound. Parser notation can evaluate arithmetic such as 1/3 before storing the bound.
Assumption state is process-wide until it is cleared or forgotten.

functions.name: transpose
functions.summary: Returns the transpose of a matrix.
description: transpose(...) swaps matrix rows and columns and returns a new matrix value.
The same operation is also available as Matrix.transpose() in the JavaScript / TypeScript object API.

examples.description: Transpose a numeric 2 by 2 matrix.
Transpose a rectangular matrix while preserving symbolic entries.

functions.name: augment
functions.summary: Horizontally joins two matrices with the same number of rows.
description: augment(left,right) appends the columns of the right matrix to the left matrix.
Both matrices must have the same number of rows.

examples.description: Append one column to a two-column matrix.

functions.name: rref
functions.summary: Returns the reduced row-echelon form of a matrix.
description: rref(...) performs row reduction and returns the reduced row-echelon form.
An optional prime modulus selects finite-field arithmetic.

examples.description: Reduce an invertible 2 by 2 matrix.

functions.name: nullspace
functions.summary: Returns a basis for the nullspace of a matrix.
description: nullspace(...) returns a Vector whose entries are basis vectors for the matrix nullspace.
The operation is available in Nerdamer Notation, on the root nerdamer API, and as a direct import from nerdamer/structures.

examples.description: Find a basis for a rank-deficient matrix.

notes: An optional second argument selects finite-field arithmetic with the supplied prime modulus.

functions.name: determinant
functions.summary: Computes the determinant of a square matrix.
description: The determinant can contain symbolic entries as well as numbers. The direct helper works on a copy of the supplied Matrix, so computing the determinant does not mutate the original matrix.
A non-square matrix does not have a determinant and is rejected.

examples.description: Compute the determinant of a 2 by 2 matrix.
The determinant of an identity matrix is 1.

functions.name: imatrix
functions.summary: Creates an identity matrix of the requested integer size.
description: For an integer n, imatrix creates an n by n Matrix with ones on the main diagonal and zeros elsewhere. A non-integer symbolic size remains as an unevaluated imatrix call.

examples.description: Create a 3 by 3 identity matrix.

functions.name: dot
functions.summary: Computes the dot product of two vectors.
description: Concrete vectors must have the same length. Their corresponding elements are multiplied and summed to produce a scalar Expression. Symbolic non-vector operands can remain as an unevaluated dot call.

examples.description: Compute a numeric three-dimensional dot product.
Reduce symbolic Vector components to an exact scalar expression.

functions.name: cross
functions.summary: Computes the cross product of two three-dimensional vectors.
description: Concrete Vector operands must each contain exactly three elements. The result is a Vector perpendicular to the two input vectors. Symbolic non-vector operands can remain as an unevaluated cross call.

examples.description: Compute the cross product of the first two standard basis vectors.
Compute a three-dimensional cross product with symbolic components.

functions.name: and
functions.summary: Returns 1 when every argument is nonzero and 0 otherwise.
description: and uses Nerdamer Scripting truthiness, where zero is false and nonzero expressions are true. Arguments are deferred and evaluation stops at the first false value.

examples.description: All nonzero arguments are true.
Stop at a false argument.

functions.name: or
functions.summary: Returns 1 when at least one argument is nonzero and 0 otherwise.
description: or uses Nerdamer Scripting truthiness, where zero is false and nonzero expressions are true. Arguments are deferred and evaluation stops at the first true value.

examples.description: Return true when one argument is nonzero.
Return false when every argument is zero.

functions.name: not
functions.summary: Returns 1 for a zero argument and 0 for a nonzero argument.
description: not applies Nerdamer Scripting truthiness to one evaluated expression.

examples.description: Negate a false value.
Negate a true value.

functions.name: xor
functions.summary: Returns 1 when an odd number of arguments are nonzero.
description: xor evaluates all arguments using Nerdamer Scripting truthiness and toggles the result for each true value.

examples.description: Three true arguments have odd parity.
Two true arguments have even parity.

functions.name: if
functions.summary: Evaluates one branch based on a Nerdamer Scripting condition.
description: The condition is evaluated first. Only the selected branch is evaluated, so errors or assignments in the unselected branch do not run.
The false branch is optional.

examples.description: Evaluate only the true branch.
Evaluate only the false branch.

functions.name: iferror
functions.summary: Evaluates a fallback expression only when the first expression throws an ordinary error.
description: The first argument is deferred. If it succeeds, its value is returned and the fallback is not evaluated. Parser control-flow signals such as return, break, and continue are not treated as ordinary errors.

examples.description: Do not evaluate the fallback when the first expression succeeds.
Evaluate the fallback after an error.

functions.name: iserror
functions.summary: Returns 1 when evaluating an expression throws an ordinary error and 0 otherwise.
description: The expression is evaluated lazily. Parser control-flow signals are allowed to continue to their enclosing scripting construct instead of being reported as ordinary errors.

examples.description: A successful expression is not an error.
Detect an evaluation error.

functions.name: block
functions.summary: Evaluates a sequence of Nerdamer Scripting expressions in order.
description: block evaluates its deferred arguments from left to right and returns the final completed result. return, break, and continue are allowed to propagate to the enclosing function or loop boundary.
At the outer parser boundary, an escaping return supplies the block result.

examples.description: Run assignments in sequence and return the last value.
Stop at a return value.

functions.name: while
functions.summary: Repeats a Nerdamer Scripting body while its condition is nonzero.
description: The deferred condition is reevaluated before every iteration. The final completed body value is returned, and a loop that never completes a body produces an empty result.
break exits the nearest loop, continue starts the next iteration, and a configurable iteration limit prevents runaway loops.

examples.description: Update parser state until the condition becomes zero.

functions.name: for
functions.summary: Runs a four-part Nerdamer Scripting loop.
description: for evaluates its initializer once, then reevaluates the condition before each iteration. After a completed body the update expression runs before the next condition check.
continue still runs the pending update; break and return skip it. The same loop-iteration limit used by while applies.

examples.description: Accumulate values across a finite loop.

functions.name: each
functions.summary: Evaluates a body once for each value in a parser container.
description: each(container,value,body) traverses a Vector, Matrix, ValuesSet, Collection, or Dictionary and binds each visited value to the supplied local variable while the body runs.
Matrices are traversed in row-major order. The iteration variable is local to each body evaluation.

examples.description: Accumulate values from a Vector.

functions.name: evaluate
functions.summary: Evaluates a parser value immediately, optionally with substitutions.
description: evaluate(value) invokes the value's existing evaluation behavior from Nerdamer Scripting.

The two-argument form accepts a Dictionary whose entries are substitutions for that evaluation only. They do not create or replace parser assignments, and they can be applied to expressions and supported structured values including SolutionSet results.
The three-argument form accepts a variable Vector and a same-length point Vector, which is useful for repeated numerical evaluation without rebuilding substitution dictionaries.

examples.description: Evaluate a numerical expression immediately.
Evaluate a structured value with Dictionary substitutions.
Store a periodic SolutionSet with : and evaluate one indexed family member by supplying the reserved _n index locally.
Evaluate from parallel variable and point Vectors.

notes: If evaluation cannot complete, evaluate returns the resolved input unchanged rather than creating a symbolic evaluate(...) node.
Dictionary substitutions are local to the evaluate call. Supplying {_n=>0} does not assign _n globally; _n remains a reserved solver-family index and _n:0 is still rejected.
When a value must be stored before evaluation, use Nerdamer Scripting assignment with :. The = operator denotes an equation and does not store a parser value.

functions.name: break
functions.summary: Exits the nearest Nerdamer Scripting loop.
description: break can only be used inside while or for. It is consumed by the nearest loop and cannot cross a symbolic-function boundary.

examples.description: Exit the loop after the first iteration.

functions.name: continue
functions.summary: Skips the remainder of the current Nerdamer Scripting loop iteration.
description: continue is consumed by the nearest loop. In a for loop, the update expression still runs before the next condition check.

examples.description: Skip the statements after continue.

functions.name: return
functions.summary: Returns a value from the current symbolic function or outer scripting block.
description: Inside a parser-defined symbolic function, return stops evaluation of the current function body and supplies its value. The outermost scripting block can also consume an escaping return.

examples.description: Stop evaluation and return 7.

functions.name: let
functions.summary: Creates temporary Nerdamer Scripting bindings for a body expression.
description: let accepts variable/value pairs followed by a body. The bindings are local to that body and prior parser values are restored afterward, which makes it suitable for function-local loop variables and temporaries.

examples.description: Evaluate a body with two local bindings.

functions.name: Chi
functions.summary: Computes the hyperbolic cosine integral.
description: Chi is the hyperbolic analogue of the cosine integral. Exact endpoint cases are simplified, numeric inputs can be evaluated, and symbolic inputs remain as Chi(x).
The implementation treats Chi as an even function on its supported principal real form; Chi(0) tends to negative infinity.

examples.description: Use the singular value at the origin.
Keep a symbolic argument unevaluated.

functions.name: Ci
functions.summary: Computes the cosine integral.
description: Ci evaluates supported numeric inputs and preserves symbolic arguments. It is treated as even on the supported principal real form.
Ci(0) tends to negative infinity, while Ci approaches zero at positive or negative infinity.

examples.description: Use the singular value at the origin.
Keep a symbolic cosine integral.

functions.name: Ei
functions.summary: Computes the exponential integral.
description: Ei evaluates supported numeric arguments and otherwise remains symbolic. The implementation uses the principal real exponential-integral behavior for real inputs.
Ei(0) tends to negative infinity; Ei approaches zero at negative infinity and positive infinity at positive infinity.

examples.description: Use the singular value at the origin.
Keep a symbolic exponential integral.

functions.name: Li
functions.summary: Computes the logarithmic integral.
description: Li evaluates supported non-negative numeric arguments and otherwise remains symbolic. The function has a logarithmic singularity at 1.
Negative numeric inputs are retained symbolically rather than forced through a real-valued numerical approximation.

examples.description: Use the singular value at 1.
Keep a symbolic logarithmic integral.

functions.name: Shi
functions.summary: Computes the hyperbolic sine integral.
description: Shi evaluates supported numeric arguments and otherwise remains symbolic. It is an odd function, so negative arguments are reduced through Shi(-x)=-Shi(x).

examples.description: Evaluate the origin exactly.
Keep a symbolic hyperbolic sine integral.

functions.name: Si
functions.summary: Computes the sine integral.
description: Si evaluates supported numeric arguments and otherwise remains symbolic. It is an odd function, and its limits at positive and negative infinity are plus or minus pi/2.

examples.description: Evaluate the origin exactly.
Keep a symbolic sine integral.

functions.name: delta
functions.summary: Represents the Dirac delta distribution.
description: For non-zero numeric inputs, delta evaluates to zero. At zero it remains symbolic because the Dirac delta is a distribution rather than an ordinary finite-valued function.
Symbolic inputs remain as delta(x), and assumptions can reduce a symbol known to be non-zero to zero.

examples.description: A non-zero numeric argument evaluates to zero.
Keep the singular point symbolic.

functions.name: dfact
functions.summary: Computes the double factorial of an expression.
description: Ordinary parsing preserves dfact as a symbolic function instead of forcing numerical evaluation. Call evaluate() when a numeric value is required; non-negative integers are then computed exactly and supported non-integers use the generalized gamma-based form.
The parser name dfact corresponds to Nerdamer's double-factorial implementation.

examples.description: Keep an integer double factorial symbolic until evaluation is requested.
Preserve the odd double factorial during ordinary parsing.

functions.name: erf
functions.summary: Computes the error function.
description: Numeric inputs are evaluated to high-precision decimal values, while symbolic inputs remain as erf(x). The function approaches 1 at positive infinity and -1 at negative infinity.

examples.description: Evaluate the origin exactly.
Keep a symbolic error function.

functions.name: erfc
functions.summary: Computes the complementary error function 1-erf(x).
description: erfc reuses the error-function implementation and subtracts its result from 1. Numeric inputs therefore evaluate whenever erf does.

examples.description: Use erfc(0)=1.
Resolve a large positive argument to zero.

functions.name: factorial
functions.summary: Computes the factorial of an expression.
description: Non-negative integers are evaluated exactly. Supported half-integers are reduced to closed forms involving sqrt(pi), and non-integer numerical evaluation can use the gamma function.
The compatibility spelling fact is an alias of factorial.

examples.description: Evaluate an integer factorial exactly.
Reduce a half-integer factorial symbolically.

functions.name: fib
functions.summary: Computes a Fibonacci number for an integer index.
description: Integer inputs are evaluated exactly, including negative indices through the negafibonacci relation. Symbolic and non-integer inputs remain as fib(x).

examples.description: Evaluate an exact Fibonacci number.
Use the negafibonacci relation for a negative index.

functions.name: gamma
functions.summary: Computes the gamma function.
description: Nerdamer evaluates supported integer, half-integer, and numeric arguments, using exact symbolic forms where available. Other symbolic arguments remain as gamma(x).
Gamma extends factorial through gamma(n)=(n-1)! for positive integers.

examples.description: Use gamma(n)=(n-1)! for a positive integer.
Use the exact half-integer value.

functions.name: heaviside
functions.summary: Computes the Heaviside step function.
description: Nerdamer uses the half-maximum convention: the result is 0 for negative inputs, 1/2 at zero, and 1 for positive inputs. Symbolic inputs remain as heaviside(x) unless assumptions determine their sign.

examples.description: Evaluate a negative argument.
Use the half-maximum value at zero.
Evaluate a positive argument.

functions.name: hypot
functions.summary: Computes the Euclidean magnitude sqrt(x^2+y^2).
description: hypot combines two components through a square root and lets Nerdamer simplify the resulting algebraic form. This is also used internally for complex magnitudes.

examples.description: Evaluate the 3-4-5 triangle.
Keep symbolic components in the magnitude.

functions.name: mod
functions.summary: Computes the remainder modulo another expression for supported numeric inputs.
description: Numeric arguments use Nerdamer's modulus implementation. Unsupported symbolic cases remain as mod(a,b), and undefined inputs such as a zero modulus are rejected.

examples.description: Compute a simple integer remainder.

functions.name: modinv
functions.summary: Computes a modular multiplicative inverse.
description: For supported integers a and m, modinv returns a value x such that a*x is congruent to 1 modulo m. The inverse only exists when the inputs satisfy the required coprimality conditions.

examples.description: Find the inverse of 3 modulo 7.
Find the inverse of 10 modulo 17.

functions.name: sinc
functions.summary: Computes the normalized sinc function, sin(x)/x.
description: Nerdamer uses the removable-singularity value sinc(0)=1 and treats sinc as an even function. Numeric inputs can be evaluated, while unresolved symbolic inputs remain as sinc(x).

examples.description: Use the conventional value at the origin.
Keep an unresolved symbolic argument in sinc form.

functions.name: isPrime
functions.summary: Tests whether an exact integer is prime.
description: Use isprime(...) in Nerdamer Notation and isPrime(...) from the JavaScript / TypeScript API.
Exact integer inputs return 1 for prime and 0 for non-prime values. Inputs that cannot be classified as exact integers remain symbolic.

functions.name: cos
functions.summary: Computes the cosine of an angle in radians.
description: Nerdamer returns exact symbolic values for common rational multiples of pi, simplifies cosine's even symmetry, and evaluates supported inverse-trigonometric compositions.

functions.name: sin
functions.summary: Computes the sine of an angle in radians.
description: Nerdamer returns exact symbolic values for common rational multiples of pi, simplifies sine's odd symmetry, and evaluates supported inverse-trigonometric compositions.

Apply sine's odd symmetry symbolically.

functions.name: tan
functions.summary: Computes the tangent of an angle in radians.

functions.name: acos

functions.name: atan
functions.summary: Computes the principal arctangent in radians.
description: Known inputs are reduced to exact multiples of pi when possible. Positive and negative infinity map to plus or minus pi/2.
